topic.readerProblem: Classify AI-related access-log requests without mistaking a claimed user agent for verified provider identity or a crawl for indexing.
topic.connection: Crawler reachability is a technical input to AI-search discoverability, while the article preserves the separate evidence needed for indexing, citation, and recommendation.

assessment: The final package distinguishes search, training, and user-triggered tokens from OpenAI and Anthropic, plus Googlebot and unknown traffic. Editorial review corrected the original GPTBot misclassification, added the missing documented search/user tokens, removed a broken Bing source, and verified the no-CIDR and reserved-CIDR paths.

checks: Opened the official OpenAI crawler documentation and corrected GPTBot to training while adding OAI-SearchBot search and ChatGPT-User user-triggered categories.
Checked Anthropic's official page for ClaudeBot, Claude-SearchBot, and Claude-User and aligned the fixture categories without inventing network ownership.

Ran the Python 3.9 analyzer without CIDRs and compared output byte-for-byte to expected-summary.csv; then ran the reserved-CIDR example and confirmed seven known token rows verify while unknowns remain not_checked.

artifacts.description: A populated synthetic combined access log using only RFC 5737 documentation addresses.
A dependency-free Python 3.9 analyzer separating claimed token, local category, and optional IP verification.
Date-stamped search, training, user-triggered, and Google token rules linked to official sources.
A reserved-address CIDR fixture that tests the verification interface without asserting provider ownership.
The checked deterministic summary for the no-CIDR synthetic run.

methodology: The analyzer parses a standard combined log, matches reviewed user-agent tokens case-insensitively, groups claims by documented purpose, and optionally checks source IPs only against an operator-supplied CIDR file. Ten synthetic rows use RFC 5737 addresses; no real provider ranges are hardcoded or inferred.
limitations: User-agent matching does not verify identity, reserved CIDRs are not provider ranges, and a logged request does not prove indexing, retrieval, citation, ranking, or recommendation.
